newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in quieter trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in quieter trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Thursday in quiet trading a day after Israel's central bank announced it would cut its key lending rate by 1.2 percentage points, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.04 pct to 107.51
* CPI-linked government bonds: unchanged at 107.26
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.12 pct to 109.08
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.07 pct to 106.00
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.09 pct to 106.97

Volume including Makams was 157 million shekels, with turnover in dollar-linked bonds falling to 16.5 million shekels from an unusually high 30 million shekels on Wednesday and 47.5 million shekels on Tuesday.
"The market calmed down today after the big rises it registered yesterday after the interest rate cut. The market has absorbed the news and found its balance," said Roy Meir of Simodan.

After the Israeli cabinet adopted a plan on Wednesday to widen the exchange rate band and adjust its diagonol rate, the central bank lowered its key lending rate to an annualised 12.7 percent. It was the first rate cut since February.
Trading in CPI-linked bonds was mixed, traders said, while demand for unlinked bonds continued. Dollar-linked bonds closed with slight price rises, they said.
"Yields of CPI-long bonds are around four percent and I believe they will stay at these levels," Meir said.
Some traders, however, said they expected yields on the bonds to fall further in coming weeks.

"Yesterday for the first time yields on CPI-linked long bonds (10 to 15 years) breached the four percent barrier and closed at 3.98 to 3.99. In the next two weeks I think we'll see yields at 3.95," said a trader.

Yields on unlinked bonds continued to fall, with one-year Makams and 36-month unlinked bonds trading at 12.5 percent, Meir said. "The yield curve is flat, which points to expectations that nominal interest rates will remain unchanged or will continue to fall," he said.
Yields on dollar-linked bonds were stable at around the seven percent, Meir said, after prices rose sharply on Wednesday.
The shekel representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar on Thursday at 3.4190 shekels versus 3.4200 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.42 shekels)
